abstract: This study analyzes 62 million U.S. resumes to examine employment changes at AI-adopting firms, finding that junior-level employment declined sharply while senior-level employment remained largely unchanged. The authors characterize this pattern as 'seniority-biased technological change,' suggesting that AI adoption has differential impacts across experience levels in the workforce.
keyFindings: Analysis of 62 million U.S. resumes reveals sharp decline in junior employment at AI-adopting firms
Senior-level employment at AI-adopting firms was largely unchanged following AI adoption
AI adoption demonstrates seniority-biased technological change patterns
methodology: Analysis of 62 million U.S. resumes tracking employment changes at firms adopting AI technology. Specific sample size, time period, and analytical approach not detailed in available excerpt.
qualifiers: Limited information available; full study details not provided in excerpt. Scope appears limited to U.S. resume data. Preliminary characterization based on available excerpt.
